Primary request: Create an ORIGINAL polished diagram explaining how a messaging system permits adding consumers. This is a new design, not a scan or redraw of any textbook page.

Exact Korean text:
Title: "메시징으로 소비자 확장하기"
Subtitle: "하나의 메시지를 필요한 시스템에 전달한다"

prompts.outbox:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: finished Korean technical blog diagram, landscape 1536 by 1024. Dense but highly readable at 750px rendered width.
Primary request: Create an ORIGINAL technical diagram explaining transactional outbox, with two clearly separated phases. Use a fresh block-flow layout, NOT a UML sequence diagram or textbook scan.
Style: pure white background, clean flat editorial infographic, dark navy Korean sans-serif type, teal and soft blue accents, rounded rectangles, generous whitespace, thin slate arrows with distinct arrowheads, no texture, gradient, shadow, or decoration. Match a modern backend engineering blog.
Composition: title at top left and short subtitle below.
UPPER PHASE: teal-tinted rounded panel labeled "1. 하나의 DB 트랜잭션". Inside, two side-by-side compact boxes, "업무 데이터 변경" and "아웃박스에 메시지 저장", with a plus sign between them. Below these boxes inside the same panel, one centered pill "함께 커밋". The panel visually groups the data change and outbox insert as ONE atomic DB transaction. A thin downward arrow from the completed upper phase goes into lower phase.
LOWER PHASE: panel labeled "2. 커밋 후 메시지 전송". Arrange three boxes from left to right: "아웃박스" with sublabel "미발송 메시지", "메시지 중계", "메시징 시스템". Draw arrow from 아웃박스 toward 메시지 중계 labelled "조회", and from 메시지 중계 to 메시징 시스템 labelled "전송". BELOW these boxes draw a returning arrow from 메시지 중계 back to 아웃박스, labelled "전송 성공 후 완료 표시". Do NOT start that returning arrow at the broker. The relay is what writes delivery-complete status to the outbox after successful send.
Exact title: "트랜잭션 아웃박스의 처리 흐름"
Exact subtitle: "업무 변경과 메시지 저장을 묶고, 전송은 따로 처리한다"
Exact other text is the quoted Korean labels in the composition.
Bottom caption: "롤백되면 업무 데이터와 메시지 저장도 함께 취소된다."
Constraints: use only this text; no watermark, source credits, book title, page number, textbook border, document screenshot, extra icons or claims. Correct flow direction is essential. Keep arrow labels off crossing lines and ensure every label fits in its box.

revisions.outbox:
Edit the provided diagram. Change ONLY the return connector in the bottom blue panel. Preserve all Korean text exactly, all fonts, all colors, all boxes, both upper and lower phases, both existing horizontal arrows, canvas size and layout.
The return connector with label "전송 성공 후 완료 표시" currently incorrectly starts from the bottom of the RIGHT box "메시징 시스템". Erase the short vertical segment below that right box and erase the horizontal segment from that right box across to the middle.
Draw the corrected return connector starting at the BOTTOM CENTER of the MIDDLE box "메시지 중계". It goes DOWN, then LEFT, then UP with an arrowhead entering the bottom center of the LEFT box "아웃박스". Thus only the message relay writes the status to the outbox. No downward or returning edge may connect to the rightmost messaging system box. The bottom return path should be confined horizontally between the left and middle boxes.
Move the existing label "전송 성공 후 완료 표시" so it sits clearly ABOVE the LEFTWARD horizontal portion of the new return connector, between the left and middle boxes, with adequate room and no overlap. Use a smaller readable label if needed.
Do not add or remove any other text, connectors, boxes, icons, or visual elements. This is a precise semantic correction of one connector, not a redesign.

Asset: crisp Korean technical-blog diagram, approximately 1536 x 1152 landscape. Balanced modest margins. Thin connectors and dashed vertical lifelines; moderate, readable Korean sans-serif labels, mostly regular or medium weight. Aim for readability at 750 CSS pixels wide. This is a diagram inside an already titled article, not a poster.

Four participants across the top in EXACT left-to-right order:
1. "업무 서비스"
2. "DB" with small second line "업무 데이터 · 아웃박스"
3. "메시지 중계"
4. "메시징 시스템"
Use small rounded participant headers, one dashed vertical lifeline descending from each. Time progresses top to bottom.

TOP transaction group: a light teal UML frame covers ONLY the service and DB lifelines and the first four rows. A small frame label reads "하나의 DB 트랜잭션". Inside this frame all four solid arrows start at the LEFT 업무 서비스 lifeline and point RIGHT into the DB lifeline, in strictly this top-to-bottom order:
"1. 트랜잭션 시작"
"2. 업무 데이터 변경"
"3. 아웃박스에 메시지 저장"
"4. 커밋"
All four operation labels sit above their arrows and fit between the service and DB, using line breaks for step 3 if needed. The transaction frame closes AFTER step 4 and BEFORE step 5. A slim DB activation bar during this group is optional.

LOWER polling group: below the commit, a separate thin light-blue UML loop frame covers ONLY the DB, message-relay, and messaging-system lifelines. It MUST NOT include the business-service lifeline. Its small label is "주기적 반복". Within this frame, use the following strictly ordered, vertically separated exchanges:
Step 5: solid arrow FROM 메시지 중계 LEFTWARD TO DB, labelled "5. 미발송 메시지 조회".
Return: dashed arrow FROM DB RIGHTWARD TO 메시지 중계, labelled "미발송 메시지". This is a return, not a new numbered step.
Step 6: solid arrow FROM 메시지 중계 RIGHTWARD TO 메시징 시스템, labelled "6. 메시지 전송".
Return: dashed arrow FROM 메시징 시스템 LEFTWARD TO 메시지 중계, labelled "전송 성공". This denotes successful handoff, not downstream business processing.
Step 7: solid arrow FROM 메시지 중계 LEFTWARD TO DB, labelled "7. 발송 완료 표시".

Critical correctness:
- Commit row 4 is visibly ABOVE every exchange in the polling frame.
- Relay reads messages from the SAME DB where the service stored the outbox.
- Both query (5) and completion update (7) are initiated by relay and point to DB.
- The broker never directly updates DB and never calls the business service.
- The successful-send return occurs before the completion update.
- Every arrow has one clear arrowhead, solid calls and dashed returns.
- Labels must not cross participant lifelines or other labels. Make enough vertical space for nine exchanges.
- Keep all exact Korean text, no new claims, no large headings.
